# Read findings: unit U1 of goal an-ask-reaches-the-holder (round 3)

Subject: the diff of goal/an-ask-reaches-the-holder against d73a6816af45fd055d47ec4da00a82542825f4f0, judged against the build brief at /Users/wido/.metasystem/unit/.inputs/473b399a831bc7b74fb882de0bf67355/build-brief.md (FINAL revision 2) and this round's follow-up (comments only).

Candidate: /Users/wido/.metasystem/unit/20261102t164341-402fe74aaa/round-3/worktree.diff.
- Its SHA-256 is ddfad414…4c5858. That equals the brief's named hash and `git diff --full-index d73a6816a` of the prepared copy, checked both before and after this read's test runs.
- The read diff (launch r3-s3) is byte-identical to it.
- `git status --untracked-files=all` shows exactly the six files of the diff, and no other file.

The previous read (round 2, r2-s4) had no material finding and four non-gating notes. Relations below refer to those notes.

## AGREE

No material finding. Every change the brief asks for is present and correct, and it is tested. Nothing outside the brief's three production files and their three test files changed.

### Round 3 against round 2

The only change between round-2/worktree.diff and round-3/worktree.diff is in `cmd/metasystem/intent_agent.go`, and it is comments only:
- the `caller` comment now says the inbox marker reads `agentHolds` instead;
- one-line comments were added on `classify`, `getenv` and `agentHolds`;
- gofmt realigned the struct fields, which follows from the new comments.

No code token changed. The follow-up's ask is met, and the previous read's note 2 is folded and holds. The comments have no history words.

### Checklist item 1: the diff against the brief

`cmd/metasystem/intent_agent.go` (section 6):
- `agentOwners` gains `classify` (default `lease.ClassifyVerbAt`) and `getenv` (default `os.Getenv`) in `withDefaults`. The zero value stays production.
- `agentClassification(inv, path)` keeps the old body's order:
  1. the job marker first, through `getenv`, giving `{DELEGATE}`;
  2. then `ResolveLayout(path)`;
  3. then one `classify(installation, installation, os.Getpid())`, where the installation is `layout.InstallationRoot.Path()`.

  It does not use `RootForInstallation`. If the layout fails, the path is both roots. An error gives the zero result.
- `agentCaller` returns `.Class`. `agentHolds` is `Class == MAIN && Holder`.
- `agentSeat` gains `path`, set from the new `agentPath(inv)`. That function is `agentCheckout`'s own input, `inv.cwd` or `--repo` made absolute, now factored out.
- The inbox uses `marks := !all && agentHolds(inv, seat.path)`, once, before printing. The comment above it says "the main session that holds the seat's lease".
- Unchanged: the N-6 note, the help, the write guard, `--all` and `board.Mark`.
- The own-engine and person checks (`own_engine.go:44`, `person_refusal.go:114`) still pass the checkout they passed before. Their `caller` stubs (`own_engine_test.go:49/80/104`, `agent_session_refusal_test.go:23/32`) are untouched.

`ClassifyVerbAt` (`internal/lease/verbs.go:379-405`) sets `Holder = MAIN && (no lease || MainId == HolderMainId)`, so `agentHolds` is exactly what the brief describes. The lease package is unchanged.

`internal/steward/situation.go`:
- `readAsks` reads `Offered(cmp.Or(thread.Root.To.Machine, s.Machine))`.
- An ask to this seat, or to a goal, reads this machine's marker as before. This seat's own ask to another seat reads that seat's marker.
- Both comments are updated.
- I found no other production reader of `SituationAsk.Delivered` besides `askLine`. The other `.Asks` hits in `internal/ui` are channel questions, a different type. The struct is unchanged, so the JSON shape is unchanged.

`internal/steward/situation_compose.go`:
- `askLine` appends `, delivered` or `, not delivered yet`, but only when all of these hold: the thread is an ask, it is from this seat, it is to a seat (not a goal), and it is open or expired.
- The shape is the brief's: "from m1e to m1x, asked …, due HH:MM, not delivered yet". It is also correct with "no deadline" and with "past its deadline …".
- `outstanding` and `firstThing` only name incoming asks, so the first thing is unchanged.
- The wake lines (`ask|id|state`) do not include `Delivered`, so `--wait` does not wake on delivery. That matches the brief's "not in this goal".

Tests:
- The agent bed (`intent_agent_test.go`) now uses the brief's `classify` stub: "" or MAIN means holder, any other class means not the holder. It also adds `getenv` returning "" and the resolver over `fakeTop(b.root)`.
- The layout bed still reads as HUMAN, so the goldens are unchanged. No testdata is in the diff, and the frozen `^TestAudit` run is ok.
- T1, T2 and T3 match section 8:
  - production `agentCheckout` (the bed's `root` is set to nil);
  - a `getenv` that fails on any key other than the job marker;
  - a classifier fixture that checks the adapters root and the pid, and records every call;
  - T1's nested case uses `<app>/tools/ms` with an empty `metasystem.conf`, the same shape as `stateroot_test.go:201`. `ResolveLayout` selects it through `installationAncestor` (`stateroot.go:235-247`).
- All new tests call `t.Parallel()`, and none uses `t.Setenv`, `time.Now` or sleep.
- No added line names a runtime or a terminal tool (R-140). The only runtime names in `intent_agent.go` are in the unchanged help text at `:215`.

Size (numstat):
- production 46+18+5+3+7 = 79 (estimate 80, stop line 250);
- tests 137+7+5+64 = 213;
- total 292, against `--lines 300`.

### Checklist item 2: the proof and the tests

- The frozen unit check (round-3/check-458317463) passed: the cheap step and the audits both passed, with `LANDING-CHECKED 0`.
  - Its selection names T1, T2 and `TestIntentAgentInboxMarksOnlyForTheSeatsAgent`, and it ran `internal/steward` whole (group `unit/internal/steward` green).
  - It ran from 2026-11-03 05:45Z. All six files were last changed before that (the latest is `intent_agent.go`, 2026-11-02 21:35Z), so the check covered this exact tree.
- This read reran the tests once, at a host load of about 11 to 12, using a scratch `TMPDIR`. All passed:
  - in `cmd/metasystem`: T1, T2, `TestIntentAgentInboxMarksOnlyForTheSeatsAgent`, `TestIntentAgentInboxMarksOnlyWhatItPrinted`, `TestIntentAgentReplyAndInbox` and `TestAgentAskReadsTheGoalsAtTheInstallationBelowTheCheckout`;
  - in `internal/steward`: T3, `TestTheSituationKeepsEveryAskOfThisSeat` and `TestTheFirstThingIsTheOldestOutstandingAsk`.
- It then applied two brief kills that the previous read had not tried, as `go test -overlay`, without touching the worktree. Both were caught:
  - "the word kept after a reply" (dropping the state guard in `askLine`): T3 fails, `situation_compose_test.go:97`, on the replied line "…, delivered";
  - "a mark on `--all`" (dropping `!all`): T2 fails, `intent_agent_state_root_test.go:183`, "all marked".
- The previous read's overlay kills cover the others: the lease read at the Git top, the layout resolved again from the Git top, MAIN without the holder test, `Delivered` read from this machine's marker, and the word on incoming asks.
- I checked the remaining two by reading the code:
  - "job marker dropped": T2's `job` case has a classifier that answers holder, so it would mark, and its `calls != 0` check also fails;
  - "mark on any caller": the `job`, `delegate`, `person` and `other main` cases would each write the marker.
- The non-happy paths are tested: job marker, delegate, person, non-holder main, classification error, `--all`, past deadline and replied.

## Non-gating observations (numbered, most severe first)

1. A holder that reads from inside a goal worktree still marks nothing. Where: `cmd/metasystem/intent_agent.go` (`agentHolds(inv, seat.path)`). RELATION: same-rule-as 1. Rule: brief section 6 (the command's own selected path) and section 10 (rare cases).
   - With the cwd inside a goal worktree, `agentPath` selects the worktree's own `metasystem` installation. Nothing is announced there; `own_engine.go:43` says a worktree's session is announced at its serving checkout. So the holder reads as DELEGATE and sees "shown, not marked read".
   - This is the behaviour from before the unit, and it is on the safe side: nothing is swallowed, and the tool gate still marks.
   - The brief chose this path on purpose, so this is not a defect of the diff. It is a candidate for the later list if holders turn out to read from goal worktrees.
2. The own-engine and person checks now read the installation's real lease and announcements. Where: `cmd/metasystem/intent_agent.go` (`agentCaller` through `agentClassification`). RELATION: same-rule-as 3. Rule: brief section 6.
   - A corrupt lease or announcement file there now gives "" where the Git top gave DELEGATE or HUMAN. The callers then treat the caller as a person: no own-engine refusal, and no "name your session".
   - The brief prescribes this behaviour ("An error gives the zero result"; `agentCaller` returns `.Class`).
   - On success, the class those callers test (MAIN or DELEGATE) is unchanged or moves from DELEGATE to MAIN, and both accept either. STEWARD and the other classes are neither MAIN nor DELEGATE in either place. The inbox fails safe.
   - It needs a corrupt file to happen, which is improbable.
3. The unit's proof command, `/usr/bin/true`, exercises nothing itself. Where: the unit's proof command. RELATION: same-rule-as 4. Rule: checklist item 2.
   - The changed behaviour is exercised by the frozen unit check and by this read's reruns and mutations above.

## Budget

Every checklist item was checked within the tool-call budget (about 20 of 48 used).

VERDICT: land
